claims.text: The identity of X (Si, Mn, or Al) controls whether a coherent protective oxide layer forms and persists above 900 °C.
X governs oxidation behavior by altering oxide phase chemistry, growth kinetics, and interfacial stress.
Si or Al additions promote continuous, slow-growing, low-defect oxide scales.
The protective scales promoted by Si or Al are silica- or alumina-enriched Cr-oxide layers.
Si- or Al-modified scales have lower thermal-expansion mismatch with the alloy substrate.
Mn promotes defect-rich or non-adherent manganese-containing oxides.
Manganese-containing oxides are more prone to cracking or spallation.
Oxide-scale morphology and phase composition mediate stress relaxation and limit diffusion-driven scale growth and spallation.
Alumina- or silica-enriched oxide constituents are thermodynamically stable and slow-growing under the proposed exposure conditions.
The oxide constituents promoted by Si and Al are coherent with the substrate.
Si- and Al-promoted oxide layers reduce thermal-expansion mismatch and act as diffusion barriers, thereby lowering oxidation kinetics.
Mn does not promote comparably protective oxide phases and consequently produces more porous and less coherent scales.
Porous, less coherent Mn-containing scales are susceptible to cracking during thermal cycling and corrosive attack.
Relative to CrFeCoNi and the Mn-containing alloy, Si- and Al-containing alloys will form thinner, more continuous, more adherent, and lower-defect oxide layers.
The Mn-containing alloy will form thicker, less coherent, and cracked or spalled oxide scales.
The proposed behavior applies above 900 °C in controlled oxidative or corrosive atmospheres for single- or multiphase metallic solid-solution alloys.
The proposed behavior may not extend to heavily segregated microstructures or alloys made with different processing histories.
Processing variation and minor phase heterogeneity may alter oxide-scale formation and persistence.

contradictions.description: The intervention defines the baseline as CrFeCoNi without X, whereas the baseline field allows either X-free CrFeCoNi or the Mn-containing alloy to serve as the reference. The predicted outcome treats the X-free baseline and Mn-containing variant as distinct comparators, so the control is not defined consistently.
